To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the following global constraints can be decomposed: Disjoint, Partition, and Intersection with cardinality constraints, and that the following constraints can be decom- posed but only at the expense of hindering the enforcement of bound consistency: Disjoint, Intersection, Partition with cardinality constraints.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of efficient global constraints for set variables.
the development of new and efficient algorithms for enforcing bound and local consistency of set and multiset constraints.
the design and analysis of global constraints that are useful in practice.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have a good understanding of the computational complexity of the global set and multiset constraints that we have studied so far.
the three global constraints on sets and multisets we consider are easy to enforce in practice, but hard to enforce in theory, and that they all have a dual viewpoint.
the three constraints are all tractable.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, for the most part, the global constraints on set variables are as powerful as the global constraints for finite variables.
the complexity of global set and multiset constraints can range from polynomial to NP-complete, depending on the type of global constraint and the type of local consistency we enforce.

we can enforce bound consistency for a large number of global constraints, and that the complexity of enforcing this level of local consistency for the remainder of the constraints is not prohibitive.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the decomposition of global constraints on sets and multisets can be exploited in order to design efficient algorithms for enforcing bound or weak consistency on the constraints themselves.
the global constraint framework provides an effective way to reason about the complexity and design of global constraints for set and multiset domains.

we can develop global constraints for set and multiset constraints that are efficient to implement and enforce, and which are as expressive as the global cardinality constraints for finite-domain constraints.
